name: doc-verbs-hardening
problem: Refusals on re-minted records name the continuation, so a half-applied round batch converges on re-run

architecture_summary.role: mints and retires doc skeletons; owns the refusal wording

scenarios: An agent's round batch dies mid-way; re-running the identical batch converges — applied lines answer with continuations, the tail lands. Runs on cargo test (a_replayed_batch_converges).

tasks.description: Re-minting the identical record converges instead of refusing: `stress open` of the already-open round (same slug) exits 0 naming it as this round; `req add` and `stress add` whose target file byte-equals the skeleton they would write exit 0 — already minted, fill the slots. Anything else stays loud: a foreign open round, a taken slug elsewhere, a standing file that moved past its skeleton all refuse with the continuation named.
tasks.stack_details:
same-record detection: open-round slug equality; existing-path equality before the slug-taken refusal
idempotence test = byte-equality with the would-be skeleton; edited files are not re-mintable

refusals-name-the-continuation: cargo test a_replayed_batch_converges — a mid-batch death replayed in full converges: applied lines answer continuations, the tail lands
cargo test a_replayed_batch_converges — `stress open` of the open round names it as this round and points at `stress add`
cargo test a_replayed_batch_converges — re-minting a standing skeleton answers that the file stands and its slots await prose
